claims.text: The as-deposited non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi-type alloy is an ordered, single-phase hexagonal material.
The as-deposited alloy undergoes a first-order magnetostructural transition.
The first-order transition in the as-deposited alloy is sharp and hysteretic.
The magnetocaloric response and hysteresis are governed by the density and distribution of microstructural interfaces.
Rapid annealing followed by quenching will induce a nanocrystalline microstructure in the alloy.
The induced nanocrystalline microstructure will increase the density of grain boundaries.
The induced nanocrystalline microstructure will form additional interphase or secondary interfaces.
Additional microstructural interfaces provide sites for strain accommodation during the magnetostructural transition.
Internal-stress buildup is responsible for the large hysteresis of the as-deposited alloy.
Interface-mediated strain accommodation alleviates internal-stress buildup.
Alleviating internal-stress buildup through nanocrystallinity will reduce magnetocaloric-cycle hysteresis relative to the untreated baseline.
The treatment may broaden the magnetic entropy-change response over temperature.
The treatment should not significantly diminish the amplitude of the magnetic entropy change.
The untreated alloy has limited heat exchange because of its low surface-to-volume ratio.
The predictions apply only when nanocrystallinity is produced without phase decomposition or unintended secondary phases.

contradictions.description: The sample is repeatedly described as as-deposited, but arc-melted ingots and melt-spun ribbons are offered as examples; these are ordinarily as-cast or as-solidified forms rather than deposited materials.

The mediator invokes secondary or interphase interfaces formed by treatment, while the boundary requires avoiding unintended secondary phases. Grain boundaries are compatible with a single phase, but secondary/interphase boundaries require clarification about permitted phase coexistence.
